title: Stable-range quantization sweeper and layer rescale automation for accuracy-preserving INT8/FP8 profiles
creator: Arielle Chen
description:
Objective: Build an automated 'sweeper' that searches stable value ranges per-layer and per-head for FP8/INT8 quantization profiles, applies conservative layer rescale fixes, and integrates calibration + accuracy validation pipelines for Llama/Mistral/Qwen families.

Background: Prior work concentrated on model-specific calibration and outlier attenuation (ENG-23789, ENG-17456, ENG-21110). We still observe model and layer-level failures during low-bit quant (INT8/FP8) caused by sporadic activation outliers and headwise distribution shifts that break symmetric quantizers and cause token-level regressions. Manual per-model tuning is slow and brittle.

Scope:
- Sweeper: automated search that proposes per-layer min/max/clipping and scale adjustments using a small, representative calibration corpus. Supports both FP8 and INT8 quant modes.
- Layer rescale automation: compute a stable rescale factor for layers with volatile activation ranges and emit a config patch that the runtime can optionally apply at load-time.
- Model-specific heuristics: presets and detectors for Llama, Mistral, and Qwen (different attention/head behaviors).
- Calibration pipeline integration: run the sweeper in the calibration harness, validate candidate profiles against held-out accuracy tests (perplexity/ROUGE/QA pass rates) and quantitative metrics (KL divergence of activation histograms, token-level distillation loss).
- Safety: conservative fallback policy (no profile promotion unless metric thresholds passed), and a canary rollout path via 'runtime-1.20-quant-canary'.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- Sweeper uses two modes: exploratory (broader range search, slower) and conservative (narrower ranges, faster). Exploratory should be used offline and conservative in CI for automatic promotions.
- We prefer layer rescale over clipping in many layers to preserve dynamic range for subsequent layers; rescale is reversible and simpler to reason about for per-token caching.
- For Llama and Mistral, headwise variance is a strong signal; we run a headwise variance detector to decide between uniform layer scale vs headwise adjustment. Qwen shows wider embedding tails; require additional clipping thresholds on first MLP layers.
- Metrics: primary validation is end-to-end accuracy regression threshold (<= 0.5% absolute drop on curated evals) and token-level cross-entropy delta (< 0.02). Secondary: throughput/regression in latency < 5%.

Implementation plan:
1) Build sweeper utility in inference/quantation/service: takes model binary, calibration corpus, and mode flag. Outputs candidate profile JSON + per-layer suggested rescale values.
2) Add heuristics module with model fingerprints (LLama/Mistral/Qwen) and default presets.
3) Hook sweeper into calibration CI: run on PRs for quant-related runtime changes, store artifacts in S3 and mark pass/fail in the PR.
4) Create validator job in eval harness: run candidate profile on a held-out eval suite (QA, summarization, next-token), compute metrics, and decide promotion.
5) Runtime support to accept 'profile-patch' metadata at model load for optional rescale application.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sweeper produces stable candidate profiles for at least 90% of test models in the calibration suite (including Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B-v0.2, Qwen-7B).
- No promoted profile causes >0.5% absolute drop on primary evals across the three model families; rollback path validated.
- Integration tests added to CI that run a representative calibration job under 'conservative' mode within 30 minutes for a 13B model.
- PR with runtime changes to support profile-patches merged and staged in runtime-1.20-canary.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Sweeper overfits to calibration corpus -> Mitigate with cross-validation over multiple calibration splits and a holdout evaluation set.
- Risk: Headwise rescaling increases model variance -> Mitigate by requiring headwise adjustments only when KL/head-variance exceeds threshold and when accuracy delta improves on validation.
- Risk: Increased serving complexity -> Keep runtime change opt-in (profile-patch), and add telemetry to track usage and errors.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- New console dashboard: quant-profile promotions, per-model acceptance rates, accuracy deltas, and fail-mode reasons (KL/CE spikes, per-layer reject).
- Runtime metric: fraction of requests served with profile-patch applied, and token error rates.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: internal sweeper experiments offline, collect artifacts and tune heuristics.
- Week 2: CI integration and validator job; run across calibration harness.
- Week 3: runtime opt-in canary (runtime-1.20-canary) with limited traffic and monitoring.
- Week 4+: gradual promotion to default if metrics stable.

Docs & artifacts: attach calibration corpus spec, baseline eval results, and API for profile-patch metadata.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Triage: scoped goal and nominated for cycle 2025-W08. Assigned to Marcus. (Arielle)

2025-02-18 - Initial sweeper prototype completed against Llama-2-13B. Exploratory mode found 12 candidate layers requiring rescale; conservative mode found 3. Observed early accuracy: exploratory had a 0.9% hit, conservative 0.1% improvement on a small QA set. (Marcus)

2025-02-22 - Experiment details uploaded: s3://redwood-quant/artifacts/ENG-24678/exp-20250222/. Added baseline histograms and per-head variance plots. Need to add cross-validation before promotion. (Marcus)

2025-02-25 - Design review with ML infra and Runtime: agreed to make profile-patch opt-in and require CI validator pass. Action: runtime PR to accept profile-patches. (Design review notes link: https://confluence.internal/redwood/ENG-24678)
2025-02-28 - PR opened for sweeper library: github.com/redwood-inference/quant/pull/283 (WIP). Blocker: calibration harness needs faster artifact ingestion. (Marcus)

2025-03-03 - Ran conservative sweeper across Mistral and Qwen canaries. Mistral: passed primary evals; Qwen: failed on first MLP layer clipping, increased headwise KL. Decided to add Qwen-specific first-mlp clipping heuristic. (Arielle)
